sanskrit: indrāgnī huve prathamau hvayāmi marutaḥ śivān | hvayāmi viśvān devān imaṃ homam avantu me ||
english: I call upon Indra and Agni, the foremost pair; I summon the beneficent Maruts; I summon all the gods — may they protect this oblation of mine.

sanskrit: tvaṃ prathamo amṛtatvam agne devo devatvaṃ prathamo jigetha | tava divi hṛdayaṃ saṃ babhūva sa naḥ śivā āpo jātavedo ni yaccha ||
english: You, O Agni, first won immortality; as a god, you first conquered divinity. Your heart was established in heaven — O Jātaveda, grant us those auspicious waters.

sanskrit: agnāv agniś carati praviṣṭa ṛṣīṇāṃ putro adhirāja eṣaḥ | tasmai juhomi haviṣā ghṛtena mā devānāṃ yūyavad bhāgadheyam ||
english: Fire moves within fire, having entered — this one is the son of the seers, the overlord. For him I offer oblation with ghee; let him not cut off his share among the gods.

sanskrit: ye devā divi ṣṭha ye pṛthivyāṃ jātavedo ya urāv antarikṣe | ye giriṣu parvateṣv apsv antas te devā aśaniṃ yāvayātha ||
english: O Jātaveda — you gods who dwell in heaven, who are on the earth, who are in the wide mid-air, who are within the mountains, the hills, and the waters — keep lightning away.

sanskrit: mitraṃ digbhiḥ kṛṇuṣva jātaveda āśābhir mitram adhipā vipaścit | mā no hiṃsīr divyenāgninā sasyāṃ yena yanti maruta spardhamānāḥ ||
english: Make friendship by the directions, O Jātaveda; make friendship by the quarters, O wise guardian. Do not harm our crops with the celestial fire with which the Maruts go forth in rivalry.

sanskrit: vidyotamāna stanayan vṛṣevaiṣi kanikradat | bhīmaḥ parjanya te rathaḥ sa u naḥ śarma yacchatu ||
english: Flashing and thundering, you advance like a bull, roaring loudly. Fearsome Parjanya, this is your chariot — may it grant us shelter.

sanskrit: ye vidyutam aśanim ā tanvanti marutaḥ salilād adhi | kṛṣyai no viśvavārāyā avadhanvā ni tanvatām ||
english: The Maruts who stretch out lightning and thunderbolt from above the flood — may they let them drop harmlessly for the sake of our all-desirable crops.

sanskrit: yo vidyutam aśanim ātaṃty antarikṣād uta vātād divaś ca | tebhyo marudbhyo namo 'stv ojase ||
english: To those Maruts who brandish lightning and thunderbolt from the mid-air, from the wind, and from heaven — homage be to them, to their might.

sanskrit: tā yantu svaraṃkṛtāḥ syonāḥ śivatamāḥ pathā | mā na indra yavaṃ vadhīr mitramenena kṛṇmahe ||
english: May they pass by, well-marshalled, gentle, and most auspicious, along their path. O Indra, do not strike down our barley — with this rite we make you our ally.

sanskrit: darbho agra oṣadhīnāṃ śatakāṇḍo ajāyata | sa devaiḥ prahito 'yam āgan svastaye vṛṣā marudbhiḥ saha saṃvidānaḥ ||
english: Darbha grass, foremost of plants, with a hundred stalks, was born. Dispatched by the gods, this bull has come for our well-being, in accord with the Maruts.

sanskrit: vṛṣākṣasyāsurasya menir asi tāṃ tvayā tathā veda karṇasya kauvidasyevamāśā | tāṃ mābhy ava gā dvādaśāhnāni vi rakṣe ||
english: You are the anger of the bull-eyed Asura; thus does Karṇa Kauvidā know you in this manner. Do not overwhelm me for twelve days — I ward it off.

sanskrit: asir me tigmasyāyasa indrāgnibhyāṃ susaṃśitaḥ | tena sedhām id āduniṃ kṛṣiṃ me māva gād iti sasyaṃ me mā vadhīd iti ||
english: My sword is of sharp iron, well-whetted by Indra and Agni. With it I drive away the troublesome thing: "Let it not go against my crops" — "Let it not strike my grain."

sanskrit: marutaḥ pari vṛṅdhi no divaḥ kṣudrebhir aśmabhiḥ | udumbarasya śākhayā vicakṣuṣā- -aśaniṃ yāvayāmasi ||
english: O Maruts, protect us from the small hailstones of heaven. With a branch of the Udumbara tree — with the far-seeing one — we drive away the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: maruto mṛḍayāta no divaḥ śukrebhir aśmabhiḥ | udumbarasya śākhayā vicakṣuṣā- -aśaṇiṃ yāvayāmasi ||
english: O Maruts, show us favor against the bright hailstones of heaven. With a branch of the Udumbara tree — with the far-seeing one — we drive away the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: vartād vartam ā krāma parvatād adhi parvatam | girau pratiśṛtā satī vṛkṣān bhaṅdhi mā yavam ||
english: Pass from whirlwind to whirlwind, from mountain over mountain. Confined as you are to the hill, shatter trees — not barley.

sanskrit: adāmnā tvā sandhyāmi yāvaṇyā paribhūrṇyā | sānau pratiśṛtā satī tṛṇaṃ bhaṅdhi mā yavam ||
english: With a tether, with a binding, with a restraint made of barley-straw I bind you fast. Confined as you are to the ridge, shatter grass — not barley.

sanskrit: uśatī nāmāsi salindā nāma | anyām āsāṃ gaccha yaṃ dviṣmas taṃ gaccha ||
english: Your name is Uśatī; Salindā is your name. Go to another of these — go to the one we hate.

sanskrit: parācīm anu saṃvataṃ parācīm anu saṃvidaṃ parācy anu ni drava | itas tvā nāśayāmasi brahmaṇā vīryāvatā ||
english: Follow the stream flowing away yonder, follow the current going away yonder, run down following what moves away. From here we drive you away with potent sacred utterance.

sanskrit: vār bhavodakaṃ bhava- -udakasyodakaṃ bhava | kṣudrāt kṣodīyasī bhūtvā- -athehy adhamaṃ tamaḥ ||
english: Become water, become moisture, become the water of waters. Having become smaller than the smallest, go now into the lowest darkness.

sanskrit: syonā bhava śivā bhava śivāc chivatarā bhava | phenān mṛdīyasī bhūtvā- -idaṃ śasyam upā cara ||
english: Be gentle, be auspicious, be more auspicious than auspicious. Having become more yielding than foam, approach this grain crop.

sanskrit: namas te astu vidyute stanayitnave | namas te agne dūre hete kṛṇmo mā no hiṃsīr dvipado mā catuṣpadaḥ ||
english: Homage to you, O lightning, O thunder. Homage to you, O Agni — we place your missile far off; do not harm our bipeds, do not harm our quadrupeds.

sanskrit: prati tvā sahasāsahaḥ sahasā prati rudhmasi | aindram idaṃ saho mahad bhūmyās tavaṃ divi śritam | aphālakṛṣṭam ā krama mā na indra yavaṃ vadhīḥ ||
english: We repel you, O overpowering one, with power; we block you with power. This great Indra-born force, resting in heaven above the earth — step onto the unploughed ground; O Indra, do not strike our barley.

sanskrit: yāḥ samudrād uccaranty utsebhyo yā nadībhyaḥ | atyantaḥ sarpo vaidyuto 'śaniṃ yāvayād itaḥ ||
english: Those waters that rise up from the ocean, those that come from springs, from rivers — may the serpent born of lightning, dwelling within, drive the thunderbolt away from here.
